summary.title: How to Make Your Code Reviewer Fall in Love with You
summary.one_liner: Learn 13 author-side practices, such as self-reviewing, writing clear changelist descriptions, scoping changes tightly, and responding quickly, that make code reviews faster and more productive.
keywords: how to prepare code for review
takeaways: Review your own diff first, ideally after a break, and automate style and test checks so reviewers don't have to.
Write a changelist description that explains what the change achieves and why, and keep each change narrowly scoped.
Separate functional, non-functional, and refactoring changes; keep tests constant while refactoring before changing behavior.
Answer reviewer confusion by improving the code or comments rather than explaining in person, and respond explicitly to each note.
Respond to feedback without defensiveness and drive reviews to completion quickly to avoid context loss and merge conflicts.
summary.summary: The article is a practical guide for developers submitting code for review, written by mtlynch. It argues that the author shapes review quality as much as the reviewer and presents 13 techniques, grouped around the principle of valuing the reviewer's time. Each technique includes personal anecdotes and reasoning, such as keeping changes small (the author breaks up changes above roughly 400 lines of production code), separating refactoring from behavior changes, and communicating review state clearly. It does not include code samples or tool-specific instructions.
